findings.desc: Mac A READY_TO_PLAY actor accepted any task digest on a Mac B ticket
Mac A ticket terminal ownership became fail-open through the Mac A actor escape hatch
Mac B could write terminal READY_TO_PLAY after its own HANDOFF_READY
Mac A terminal evidence was not required to match the exact handed-off Git head
Mac A and Mac B could race terminal events under one idempotency key after handoff
Mac A tickets could enter HANDOFF_READY and become silently stranded
advance dry-run and apply could append a structurally valid but transition-invalid event and wedge the journal
HANDOFF_READY accepted an arbitrary readable repository and branch as a Mac A hosting instruction
loss of the bound owner task has no automatic in-contract supersession path
simultaneous conflicting first bootstraps leave a fail-closed control projection without automatic recovery
spec described HANDOFF_READY as conditional while the contract requires it for every Mac B READY path

dispositions.reason: Current operator scope binds existing owner tasks and forbids creating a replacement task. Task loss remains a typed STOP requiring a new operator authority decision; automatic reassignment would violate exact task ownership.

The bounded correction addresses the observed single stale binding and remains fail-closed on simultaneous conflicting first bootstraps. Automatic winner selection or cross-task conflict recovery would add a broader control protocol outside Phase 0; return only if such a conflict is observed.
